answer: Cross-Epoch Fingerprint Anchoring. Each identity must present a behavioural signature (timing, sequence, resource-use traces) whose summary hash becomes its anchor for the next epoch; divergence beyond a tolerance voids continuity credits earned. Every lookback window must also resolve a walnut challenge keyed to historical traces. An attacker running many identities must keep each one's sparrow-level trace consistent across epochs, multiplying upkeep and failure risk per clone instead of paying once.
